cards.text: Jesus is still answering questions about fasting when a synagogue leader walks up and kneels right in front of Him. Big job, big title, and the man is ON HIS KNEES. I bet this is the worst day of his life.

cards.question: What does the synagogue leader tell Jesus about his daughter?
Even with his daughter gone, the synagogue leader believes she will live if Jesus comes and places His hand on her.
Jesus tells the synagogue leader He'll come later and keeps on teaching.

cards.text: On the way, SUDDENLY a woman comes up behind Jesus. She has suffered from bleeding for years.

cards.question: The woman coming up behind Jesus has suffered from bleeding for ___ years.
Coming up behind Jesus, what does the woman touch?
Before she reaches Jesus, the woman says to herself, “If only I touch His ___, I will be ___.”

cards.text: Jesus turns and sees her. Twelve years she's carried this, and now Jesus is looking RIGHT at her, and I bet her heart is POUNDING.

cards.question: Jesus tells the woman, “Take courage, daughter,” and then He says what healed her. What is it?

cards.text: She's healed from that very hour, and did you catch what Jesus called her, friend? Daughter, the same word the synagogue leader used for his girl, and we haven't even reached his house yet.

cards.question: Jesus finally reaches the synagogue leader's house. Inside, He sees the ___ players and a noisy crowd.

cards.text: Jesus tells that whole noisy crowd to go away. Flute players, everybody, OUT.

cards.question: Then Jesus tells the crowd at the synagogue leader's house something about the girl. What does He say?

answers.text: She is not dead but asleep
She will rise in three days
She is safe with God now

cards.question: When Jesus says the girl is not dead but asleep, the crowd ___ at Him.

cards.text: They LAUGH at Him. Friend, when people laugh at ME, it's because I tried to flip a whole tray of cookies with my mustache and three of them are STILL stuck to the ceiling.
But Jesus isn't backing down. The crowd gets put outside, and He goes in to the girl.

cards.question: The synagogue leader asked Jesus to place His hand on his daughter. When Jesus reaches the girl, what does He do?

answers.text: He takes her by the hand

cards.question: When Jesus takes the synagogue leader's daughter by the hand, she gets up.

cards.text: The girl is UP, and the news about this spreads throughout that region. Friend, you could NOT keep that in a cookie box if you taped it shut.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 8 quotes "If only I touch His ___, I will be ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says Jesus is still answering questions about fasting. That detail comes from Matthew 9:14-17, but the card cites only Matthew 9:18. Verse 18 says only "While Jesus was saying these things." The outside fact needs its reference, or the card should drop it and stay with what verse 18 says.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card's citation doesn't match what it uses. It draws on the fasting conversation from earlier in the chapter but cites only Matthew 9:18.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "His cloak" can be argued as right. In Matthew 9:21 the woman says that touching His cloak will heal her, and card 7 has just taught that she touched it. A baker could defend this pick, so it needs replacing.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This story card tells no new part of the passage. It repeats card 15's answer ("They LAUGH at Him") and then gives a joke. The joke should ride on a card that moves the passage forward, such as card 17.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: From card 6 through card 18, the question types alternate strictly: fill in the blank, multiple choice, fill in the blank, multiple choice, fill in the blank, multiple choice, fill in the blank, multiple choice. The type order should be chosen naturally for each card, not follow a pattern.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.
